title: Bridging Data-Rich and Data-Poor Domains on Lithium-Ion Battery via Scanning Electron Microscopic Data Through Convolutional Neural Network Transfer Learning
experiments_summary: SEM images were captured from NCM cathode samples (NCM333, NCM622, NCM811) across three cycling states (pristine, formation-aged, 100 cycles) at 500x magnification and 20 kV, yielding 1,700 images before augmentation. Samples were split into additive-free (E1) and additive-containing (E2) groups. An 80:20 train-test split was used, with 5-fold cross-validation on the training portion. Class imbalance was addressed by oversampling all classes to 201 samples per class. Augmentation (random cropping, flipping, rotation, and composites) expanded the dataset to 3,211 images. All models used EfficientNet-B0 as the backbone initialized with ImageNet-pretrained weights and fine-tuned with the final classification layer replaced to match nine target classes. Input images were resized to 224x224, trained with mini-batch size 16, Adam optimizer at learning rate 0.001, for a single epoch per stage, repeated ten times to report averaged results. Four training strategies were compared: (1) Pre+FT(OS): pretraining on E1 then fine-tuning on E2 with oversampling; (2) Pre+FT(WL): same but using weighted cross-entropy loss instead of oversampling; (3) FT(OS): direct training on E2 with oversampling and no E1 pretraining; (4) Pre Only: pretraining on E1 and testing directly on E2 without fine-tuning. An ablation study compared four CNN backbones—EfficientNet-B0, ResNet-18, MobileNet-v2, and DenseNet-201—under the same Pre+FT(OS) strategy, reporting accuracy, F1 score, and training time. Model interpretability was assessed using Grad-CAM visualizations to identify spatially attended regions in SEM images. All experiments were conducted in MATLAB R2024b on a system with an Intel i5-12400, 12 GB RAM, and NVIDIA RTX 3060 GPU.
